newsitem.title: IRAN: Police said to arrest Iran oil workers.
newsitem.headline: Police said to arrest Iran oil workers.

text.p: Iranian police Sunday arrested busloads of oil workers who staged a demonstration at the oil ministry to press for higher wages, witnesses said.
"Police in riot gear arrested and took away four or five busloads of protesting workers," one witness said.
"The rest of the protesters dispersed peacefully. Police continue to guard the ministry," he said.

Witnesses earlier said more than 1,000 workers from Tehran refinery, Iran's third largest, took part in the protest at the ministry in the centerre of the capital as their representatives were inside the building to negotiate with officials.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA said the workers ended their protest and returned to work after their representatives reached agreement with officials.

An employee at the ministry, who was not involved in the protest, said protesters told him more workers from Iran's main refinery in Abadan, 625 miles southwest of Tehran, were expected to come to the capital to join the protests.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.

The Tehran refinery workers were protesting at the failure of officials to deliver on promises made last month to meet some of their demands for pay rises, food coupons and housing loans, the employee told Reuters.
The workers were also protesting against pressures put on their leaders to resign from their posts at the refinery's union, said the employee.
IRNA said "tens" of workers from the Tehran refinery were at the protest. It did not say whether work at the refinery, which has a capacity of 225,000 barrels a day, had been affected.

It quoted an unnamed oil ministry official as saying "the just demands of the workers were referred to the respective departments within the ministry in the past few days to be met and both sides reached a settlement over those impractical demands made by the workers."
"He said one of the impractical demands made by workers was that they be paid equally with the civil servants of the oil ministry," IRNA reported.
